answer: Correlation penalties work like a prism: they split an agent's activity into timing, wording, and voting signals, then compare those spectra across accounts. When a cluster of new identities moves in lockstep, like weeds sprouting in one patch of a meadow, rewards for the whole cluster shrink in proportion to their similarity. An attacker tending a garden of fake agents must pay to make each one behave independently, which erases most of the profit from duplicating them.
